If a particle moves with constant acceleration $a,$ the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
r={r}_{0}+ut+\frac{1}{2}a{t}^{2},
$$

where ${r}_{0}$ is the initial position of the particle and $u$ is its initial velocity.

In our case, we have

$$
{r}_{0}=0i+0j,\,u=6i+8j,\,a=-2i-10j.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the particle after $t=1\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =(0i+0j)+(6i+8j)(1)+\frac{1}{2}(-2i-10j)(1)^{2} \\  & =(6i+8j)+\frac{1}{2}(-2i-10j) \\  & =(6i+8j)+(-1i-5j) \\  & =(\,5\,i+3\,j)\,\text{m}.\end{aligned}
$$
